data.overview: ACE gains become clearer under aggressive skipping. Qwen3.6 at 50% reaches PPL 8.67 / avg accuracy 75.57 versus MoDES 9.42 / 71.42. At 60% it remains 9.98 / 70.70. A100 measurements show actual latency gains, not only reduced expert count.

key_results.interpretation: quality gap persists at aggressive budget.
ties best external PPL and has highest average accuracy.

negative_results.name: low-sparsity exception
negative_results.description: Qwen3.6 at 10%: router Score avg 81.66 > ACE 81.41.

negative_results.name: RCR alone weak
negative_results.description: Qwen3-30B at 50%: RCR 11.62/67.01 vs GSP 8.99/74.10 because one router prototype does not represent full conditional input distribution.

negative_results.name: workload-matched threshold
negative_results.description: reported budget mapping uses an unlabeled workload score pass; threshold transfer is future work.

negative_results.name: single-run uncertainty
negative_results.description: single deterministic seed; repeated-run uncertainty is future work.

negative_results.name: distributed serving missing
negative_results.description: distributed expert dispatch is future work.

data.interpretation: ACE is a safer selection rule at fixed expert-execution budget rather than a new router. GSP supplies the dominant global signal and RCR protects directionally specialized experts.
data.quality_impact: Lossy; generally better retention than baselines at equal skip ratio, with low-sparsity exceptions and threshold-transfer uncertainty.
